title: The Profiler Says Nothing Broke
objective: Diagnose why the hot loop regressed by inspecting counters, then commit to exactly one root cause.
briefing:
A routine profiling pass shows the hot loop of your ingest-loop service has regressed measurably since yesterday's build.

The change list mentions a data-layout tweak and a library bump, neither of which touches this loop's code path.

The machine has a 16 KiB, 64 B-line, 2-way set-associative cache where the loop lives. Nothing else changed.

You have a fixed evidence budget: each probe costs a full profiling rerun. Diagnose the single root cause and commit.

actions.label: Read perf counters
actions.description: Cycle counts for the current build vs the last known-good build.

actions.label: Dump cache configuration
actions.description: Size, line size, associativity of the level the loop runs against.

actions.label: Miss-rate timeline
actions.description: Miss rate across eight equal windows of the regression run.

actions.label: Line-churn analysis
actions.description: Where repeated accesses land: which lines and sets absorb the churn.

actions.label: Coherence probe
actions.description: Cross-core invalidations vs local writes in the hot region.

hypotheses.label: Working set exceeds cache
hypotheses.detail: The active data now exceeds total cache size, so each sweep over it evicts lines still needed on the next sweep.

hypotheses.label: Cache set conflicts
hypotheses.detail: The new layout maps the hottest lines onto one cache set; associativity cannot hold them, so every pass evicts the line the next iteration needs.

hypotheses.label: False sharing between cores
hypotheses.detail: Two cores write different variables that share one cache line; ownership ping-pongs and every write pays a coherence transfer.

hypotheses.label: Useless prefetch traffic
hypotheses.detail: The access order defeats the next-line prefetcher; its issued lines are never demanded and crowd real misses on the bus.

solution.explanation: The active data now exceeds total cache size, so each sweep over it evicts lines still needed on the next sweep.
